items.item_text: Bachelor's degree in Biology or a related life science, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant laboratory experience.
At least one year of experience in a research laboratory with autoclaving, preparing reagents, basic molecular biology techniques
At least one year of experience in a research laboratory with autoclaving, preparing reagents, basic molecular biology techniques.

The Department of Molecular & Medical Pharmacology is looking to hire a Staff Research Associate 1 to support vaccine development research. This position will assist with daily laboratory operations, including cleaning and maintenance, washing and sterilizing glassware, preparing reagents, restocking supplies, autoclaving, and proper disposal of biohazardous waste. The incumbent will also support graduate students and senior scientists with laboratory experiments, including nucleic acid isolation, cell culture, transfection, Western blotting, ELISA, PCR, as well as data collection and analysis. This role is supervised by a graduate student and the Principal Investigator (PI).

the final candidate who accepts an offer of employment will be required to disclose if they have been subject to any final administrative or judicial decisions within the last seven years determining that they committed any misconduct; or have filed an appeal of a finding of substantiated misconduct with a previous employer.
Demonstrated knowledge of basic molecular biology, immunology, and biochemical principles.
Ability to use basic laboratory equipment, including centrifuge, pH meter, incubators, tissue culture hoods, ELISA reader, imager, and electrophoresis apparatus.
Ability to create and maintain records accurately.
Demonstrated computer skills including knowledge of MS Excel, MS Word and Graphpad.
Ability to communicate effectively to convey experimental results.
Interpersonal skills to effectively interact with faculty, research scientists, and students.
Ability to understand and perform a variety of routine cleaning and maintenance procedures.
Skills in using BSL2 laboratory practices and sterile techniques.
Skills in performing western blots, cell culture, and ELISA.
